multiplayer.exit.switch_failed: Exit node was not changed; multiplayer session ended: {0}
multiplayer.exit.switching: Switching: Your internet traffic will go through {0}'s computer ({1}). They must first enable “Allow members to use my computer for internet access”, or you will temporarily lose internet access. Select “Stop” to restore it.
multiplayer.exit.warning: Note: Members who choose you as their exit node will send all their internet traffic through your computer and network. It will appear to come from your IP, and you are responsible for that traffic. It also uses your bandwidth. Only enable this for people you trust.
multiplayer.host.hint: Enter a world, then select “Open to LAN” in the pause menu. Games launched with Amber appear here automatically. For games from other launchers, select “Find”.

multiplayer.join.title: Join a friend's room
multiplayer.lan.full_mode_hint: Usually unnecessary. The default mode forwards only the game port and needs no administrator access. This mode creates a virtual network adapter named “Amber LAN” and gives each member a virtual IP, letting other LAN games and apps communicate too. Game LAN broadcasts are also forwarded to room members. Windows asks for permission when creating or joining a room. The adapter shuts down when the session ends or Amber closes. Both sides must enable this mode.
multiplayer.lan.not_found: No games open to LAN found. Enter a world, select “Open to LAN” in the pause menu, then select “Find”.
multiplayer.lan.opened: {0} is open to LAN on port {1}. You can now create a room.
multiplayer.lan.port_placeholder: Or enter the port manually (shown in the game's chat)
multiplayer.lan.port_required: Select “Open to LAN” in the game first, or enter the port manually
multiplayer.lan.port_unavailable: No game is listening on local port {0}. Make sure the world is open to LAN and the port is correct.
multiplayer.lan.scan_failed: Could not find LAN games: {0}. You can also enter the port manually.
multiplayer.lan.scan_tooltip: Listen for local LAN broadcasts to find games opened by other launchers. Windows may ask for firewall permission; either choice allows local discovery.
multiplayer.matrix.completed: All-condition test complete: {0}/{1} passed. Select “Export diagnostic report” to share the results.
multiplayer.matrix.hint: Once a friend joins, test every combination in sequence with one click (IPv6, mapped ports, hole punching, port spraying, relaying, relay nodes; default and full LAN modes; exit node on/off). Records connectivity, time taken, latency, throughput, and failure reasons. Both sides switch together automatically, with a timeout for each step.
multiplayer.matrix.include_full_lan: Include full LAN mode and exit nodes (both sides approve administrator access once at the start; skipped if declined)
multiplayer.matrix.peer_required: A friend must join through a direct connection before running the all-condition test
multiplayer.matrix.requesting_admin: All-condition test: Both sides need to approve administrator access first (asked once)…
multiplayer.matrix.title: All-condition test
multiplayer.network.cone: Hole punching is likely to work: Direct connections are possible with most networks
multiplayer.network.open: Easy to connect: You're directly reachable; friends do not need to send a reply code
multiplayer.network.symmetric: Hole punching is difficult: Strict NAT and no IPv6. A typical home connection on the other side may work; if both sides have strict NAT, relay nodes are needed.
multiplayer.network.symmetric_ipv6: IPv4 has strict NAT, but you have IPv6. Direct connection is possible if the other side also has IPv6.
multiplayer.network.unknown: Could not determine: STUN did not respond; UDP may be blocked
multiplayer.nodes.added: Relay node added. Takes effect the next time you create or join a room.
multiplayer.nodes.exported: Relay node share code copied. Using the same relay nodes as your friends makes it easier to connect.
multiplayer.nodes.hint: Both sides connect to the same relay node to find each other, then connect directly if possible. Otherwise, the relay node relays traffic. Amber has no servers of its own or built-in relay nodes. Use a relay node you host (one-click deployment scripts are in the project's relay node folder), or import a friend's relay node share code.
multiplayer.nodes.host_required: No relay nodes yet. Add one under “Relay nodes” below (self-hosted, or import a friend's relay node share code). Both sides must use the same relay node.
multiplayer.nodes.invalid_address: Invalid relay node address: {0} (expected a format like tcp://example.com:11010)
multiplayer.nodes.invalid_share_code: Relay node share code not recognized. Paste a code starting with AMBNODE-, or paste a relay node address directly.
multiplayer.nodes.join_required: No relay nodes yet. Add the host's relay node under “Relay nodes” below (ask the host to export and send you their relay node share code).
multiplayer.nodes.title: Relay nodes
multiplayer.peers.title: Room members
multiplayer.proxy.allow: Allow members to forward game traffic through my computer (games only)
multiplayer.proxy.allow_warning: Games the other person launches from Amber use your network for session checks and server connections (IPv4 only). Administrator permission is not required. They cannot reach your computer, router, or home devices through you, or send email, but they can reach other public addresses (and can access other websites if they modify the program). Others see your IP, so enable this only for people you trust.
multiplayer.proxy.banner: For games launched from Amber, HTTP requests (session checks when joining servers and skins) go through the computer and network at {0}. The server entered in “Join server” on the launch page also uses it (IPv4 only). Other servers selected from the in-game server list connect directly. Domain names are resolved on your computer, and Amber refreshes its own login directly.
multiplayer.proxy.peer_label: Route game traffic through this person's network (games only)
multiplayer.proxy.restart_failed: Could not restart the multiplayer component:
multiplayer.proxy.start_tip: The other person must first enable “Allow members to forward game traffic through my computer”. The multiplayer component restarts for a few seconds, and chat reconnects automatically. This applies to games you launch from the launch page afterward.
multiplayer.proxy.stopped: Game traffic forwarding stopped. Games launched afterward will connect directly.
multiplayer.proxy.switching: Game traffic will go through {0}’s computer ({1}). They must first enable “Allow members to forward game traffic through my computer”. This applies to games launched from the launch page afterward.

multiplayer.room.code_hint: The room code contains a room key. Share it only with people you want to play with. Keep the game running and the world open to LAN.
multiplayer.room.connected: Connected to host{0}. Add server {1} in the game, or use the button below to join directly.

multiplayer.room.not_connected_hint: Not connected to the host yet. Check that the room code is complete (including the initial AMB- and mode segment), both sides use the same relay node, and both have the same version of Amber (tunneling modes require v0.5.7 or later).
